For any owner and any target and amount, if the owner mints tokens to the target, then the target's balance must increase by at least the minted amount; the bug increases totalSupply without increasing the target's balance.
After any call to mintToken, totalSupply must increase by exactly the mintedAmount; the buggy version always adds 0, violating the invariant for any non-zero mint.
After minting, the sum of all balances equals totalSupply. The bug fails to increase totalSupply, so for any nonzero mint the invariant is broken.

After mintToken(target, amount), balanceOf[target] increases by amount in the correct contract, but in the buggy version balanceOf[target] does not increase while balanceOf[owner] increases by amount instead.
In the correct version, totalSupply should always equal the sum of all balanceOf entries, but the buggy version decreases totalSupply while increasing balanceOf, breaking this invariant.
In the correct contract, totalSupply never decreases due to a mint, but the buggy one decreases totalSupply, so after any mint the totalSupply must be at least as large as it was before.
After any call to mintToken, the increase in totalSupply must equal the mintedAmount. The bug adds zero instead, so for any nonzero mintedAmount totalSupply will not track the sum of balances.
After any mintToken call, totalSupply must equal the sum of all balanceOf entries; the buggy version fails to update totalSupply, so the sum of balances exceeds totalSupply.

For any mint, totalSupply must be at least the balanceOf of the target address after minting; the buggy version omits the totalSupply update, so totalSupply remains zero and is strictly less than the target's balance for any positive mint.

After any mintToken call, the totalSupply must be >= the sum of the two highest balances (target and owner); the buggy version fails to update totalSupply, so for any positive mint to a non-owner, totalSupply stays 0 and is strictly less than this sum.
After mintToken, totalSupply equals the sum of all balanceOf entries, which the bug violates by adding an extra 1 to totalSupply.
After mintToken, the sum of all balanceOf values must equal totalSupply; the bug breaks this because totalSupply is not increased.

After calling mintToken for any non-zero mintedAmount by the owner, the totalSupply must increase by exactly mintedAmount; the mutant fails because it omits the totalSupply increment, so totalSupply stays unchanged.

Only the owner can mint tokens: any mintToken call by a non-owner leaves totalSupply and balanceOf unchanged. The buggy version allows any caller to mint, thus increasing totalSupply and target balance.
